source: Quiz 5 - Sessions 1-6: Model Training, Alignment, and the Agent Harness
question: What makes verification different from permission checking?

options.text: Verification authorizes actions; permissions judge completed results
options.feedback: This reverses their roles. Permissions constrain what may execute, while verification checks whether results satisfy the task.

options.text: Verification checks fluency; permissions check factual accuracy
options.feedback: Fluent text can still be wrong or incomplete. Permissions govern executable actions rather than factual accuracy.

options.text: Verification checks model size; permissions check the task instructions
options.feedback: Model size is not the definition of result verification. Access controls govern allowed operations, and results must be checked against the task.

options.text: Verification assesses results; permissions govern allowed actions
options.feedback: An action can be permitted and still produce an incorrect or incomplete result. These checks therefore serve different purposes.
